speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether he can provide an update on measures taken to rehabilitate and protect at-risk individuals and offenders to transform their lives and the results to date.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we intervene upstream to address risk factors before offences are committed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In 2012, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) appointed two Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to run "Youth GO!".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under Youth GO!, youth workers would conduct street outreach to engage at-risk youths and, sometimes, it could be even late at night.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This programme supports youths who are at risk of dropping out and those who have left school, so that they can continue their education or acquire vocational skills for employment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF is also working with our partners to pilot a Localised Community Network (LCN) in Jurong West, to improve the coordination among various partners and provide more seamless support to the youths and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If this pilot works out, we can look to expanding it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we divert youth offenders away from the criminal justice system as far as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF appointed nine SSAs to be what we call "Integrated Service Providers" (ISPs) which support youth offenders diverted away from the criminal justice system.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, we prioritise community-based interventions to involve families and minimise disruption to the youth's development.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Such interventions include probation and rehabilitation outside of residential facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF employs a family-focused approach to address the root causes of youth offending, such as weak family support.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The average three-year recidivism rate of probationers aged below 16 has fallen.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF's Youth Homes run programmes to build our youths’ character and lifeskills.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Formal education is a key component as well, and the majority of those who sit for national examinations, such as the GCE "N" and "O" levels, attain passes above the national average.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The longer duration helps youths to sustain good habits and skills acquired during their residence and encourages them to continue their academic or vocational training.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Singapore Prison Service adopts a similar approach for youth offenders in prison, by staging support from the point of imprisonment to their release and reintegration back into the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Government is committed to protecting and supporting youths-at-risk and youth offenders.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MSF will continue to work closely with other Ministries and our community partners to steer at-risk youths away from negative behaviours and provide rehabilitative and post-care initiatives to break the cycle of offending.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Indeed, I am very encouraged by the good progress that he has reported.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Beyond all the efforts taken, both upstream and downstream, and attempts to reintegrate these at-risk individuals with their families and into society, I would like to ask what efforts are being made, in particular, for them once they are able to get into the job market.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What efforts are there that are made to help them find suitable jobs?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: At the same time, are there any schemes which would allow employers to also be encouraged or incentivised to take on board these individuals?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Sometime ago, we ran a pilot, working with the employment agencies in the Government to provide a framework to help at-risk youths and youth offenders reintegrate into the workforce, and to help address any concerns that they may have in doing so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the conclusion of the pilot, that effort was merged into the mainstream Workforce Singapore (WSG) framework so that employment agencies working with WSG are empowered to provide better support to at-risk youths and youth offenders.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We continue to keep a close eye on that front.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: With the support of the various SSAs in the community, we will partner and look out for youths who start to struggle, even as they attempt to reintegrate back into society and back into the workforce.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We would, of course, be very happy if the Member representing the enterprises that he does, is prepared to partner us in some future point in time, to continue this work of partnership to better enable youth offenders to find their place back in society.
